prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of the UK Conservative Party Manifesto 2019 (≤500 words)

Core message
- “Get Brexit Done” with Boris Johnson’s deal: leave the EU in January 2020; no extension beyond December 2020. Outside the single market, customs union and ECJ; no political alignment. Pursue new free trade agreements (USA, Australia, New Zealand, Japan) aiming for 80% of UK trade covered in 3 years. Up to 10 freeports.

Economy and tax
- Invest while controlling debt: public net investment capped at 3% of GDP; debt lower by end of Parliament; reassess if debt interest hits 6% of revenue.
- No rises in income tax, VAT or National Insurance; raise NI threshold to £9,500 (ambition: first £12,500 tax-free).
- Maintain pension triple lock; end benefit freeze; improve Universal Credit; cut benefit fraud.
- National Living Wage to two-thirds of median earnings by 2024; £1bn for wraparound childcare; consumer protections on energy/water.
- Business support: review and cut business rates (relief for retail, pubs, venues); clamp down on late payments; expand start-up loans; strengthen anti-avoidance/evasion laws; maintain R&D incentives and raise R&D tax credit to 13%.

NHS and social care
- Record funding (c. £34bn extra by 2023/24); 40 new hospitals (plus 20 upgrades); 50,000 more nurses; 6,000 more GPs and 6,000 other primary care professionals; 50m extra GP appointments.
- NHS Visa; fix pension taper issue; Innovative Medicines Fund; mental and physical health parity; free hospital parking for those in greatest need.
- Clamp down on health tourism; NHS not “on the table” in trade talks.
- Social care: £1bn extra each year; cross-party reform with a guarantee no one has to sell their home to pay; carers’ leave; double dementia research.

Education and skills
- £14bn extra for schools; minimum per-pupil funding; teacher starting salary to £30k; support discipline and Ofsted; arts premium; more SEND funding.
- £3bn National Skills Fund; apprenticeships on major projects; £2bn FE estate upgrade; 20 Institutes of Technology; UK Shared Prosperity Fund (incl. £500m for skills).

Crime and justice
- 20,000 more police; tougher sentencing (end automatic halfway release for serious crimes; whole-life terms for child murderers); knife crime orders; 10,000 more prison places; stronger parole and a criminal justice Royal Commission.
- National cyber crime force and crime lab; victims’ law; Domestic Abuse Bill; online harms regulation; stronger powers on unauthorised traveller camps.

Infrastructure, regions and digital
- “Infrastructure revolution”: Northern Powerhouse Rail (Leeds–Manchester first), Midlands Rail Hub, major roads, EV charging network, restore some Beeching lines, superbus networks, cycling fund and standards; HS2 under review.
- Gigabit broadband nationwide by 2025 with £5bn for hard-to-reach areas.
- Towns Fund, Safer Streets Fund, cultural capital, Community Ownership Fund; English Devolution White Paper; City/Growth Deals UK-wide.

Housing
- Target 300,000 homes/year; at least 1m more over Parliament. Long-term fixed-rate mortgages for first-time buyers; discounted homes for locals/key workers; shared ownership and leasehold reform.
- End “no fault” evictions; lifetime tenancy deposits. Planning “infrastructure first”; building safety post-Grenfell; tree-lined streets; surcharge on non-resident buyers; end rough sleeping by 2024.

Rural, farming, fishing
- Replace CAP with “public money for public goods”; buy British in public sector; expand seasonal workers scheme.
- Leave CFP; sustainable fisheries; coastal regeneration; rural transport, broadband and policing.

Environment and climate
- Net Zero by 2050; 40GW offshore wind by 2030; CCUS cluster by mid-2020s; £9.2bn for energy efficiency; £4bn for flood defences; EV phase-out consultation; fracking moratorium.
- £640m Nature for Climate Fund (trees/peat); plastics measures, deposit return scheme, ban plastic waste exports to non-OECD.

Constitution and democracy
- Voter ID; equalised constituencies; keep FPTP; voting age 18; repeal Section 40/Leveson 2; Commission on Constitution, Democracy & Rights; update Human Rights Act/judicial review balance.

Defence, foreign policy and aid
- Exceed NATO 2% with 0.5% real-terms rises; modernise forces; Trident; cyber and Space Command; veterans’ support and protections.
- Magnitsky sanctions; 12 years girls’ education; maintain 0.7% aid; promote media freedom and tackle modern slavery.

Animal welfare
- Tougher cruelty sentences; animal sentience law; curb long transport for slaughter; extend ivory ban; ban primates as pets; tackle puppy smuggling; strengthen cat protections.
